title: EU AI Act: Conformity and market access

modules.title: Define the release and assessment boundary
Verify the assessor and its scope
Carry out and maintain the assessment
Complete and defend the release record

concepts.name: Market access map
concepts.assessment: Identify the distinct roles of assessment, declaration, marking and registration.

concepts.name: Assessed system identity
concepts.assessment: Specify intended purpose, version, boundaries, dependencies and release form for one system.

concepts.name: Provider release duty
concepts.assessment: Identify the provider accountable for the proposed market release or own-use putting into service.

concepts.name: High risk route
concepts.assessment: Separate Annex III, Annex I Section A, Annex I Section B and a documented non-high-risk conclusion.

concepts.name: Prohibited use precheck
concepts.assessment: Reject the inference that an assessment or a certificate can authorise an Article 5 prohibition.

concepts.name: Provision specific timeline
concepts.assessment: Distinguish Section 4 and Section 5 application from the later Section 1–3 dates; flag a case needing temporal interpretation.

concepts.name: Existing system transition
concepts.assessment: Apply the existing-system transition conditions to dated case facts without inventing universal grandfathering.

concepts.name: Sector assessment boundary
concepts.assessment: Choose the relevant sector procedure and identify its AI requirements, conditional third-party option and transitional assessor evidence.

concepts.name: Dual route priority
concepts.assessment: Select the sector procedure where the same system falls under both Annex I Section A and Annex III.

concepts.name: Requirement evidence matrix
concepts.assessment: Map an applicable requirement to evidence, an owner, a gap and a release decision.

concepts.name: Technical file index
concepts.assessment: Locate a missing system-specific record in the technical-file index; distinguish an index from proof of conformity.

concepts.name: Release scope case
concepts.assessment: Produce a dated scope record for fictional HR and medical-product releases with explicit unknowns and sources.

concepts.name: Official Journal citation check
concepts.assessment: Verify the exact standard, version, Official Journal citation, restrictions and relevant scope.

concepts.name: Limited presumption
concepts.assessment: Limit a presumption of conformity to the requirements actually covered by its legal basis.

concepts.name: Standard coverage matrix
concepts.assessment: Compare cited standard coverage with each applicable requirement and mark uncovered requirements.

concepts.name: Alternative conformity evidence
concepts.assessment: Specify evidence for a requirement outside a presumption without treating voluntary standards as the only permissible solution.

concepts.name: Common specification trigger
concepts.assessment: Distinguish a formally adopted common specification from a draft, guidance or an industry document.

concepts.name: Equivalent technical solution
concepts.assessment: Identify the justification and equivalent technical evidence needed when not complying with a common specification.

concepts.name: Contextual data presumption
concepts.assessment: Identify the limited Article 10(4) presumption for data reflecting the intended geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting.

concepts.name: Cybersecurity presumption
concepts.assessment: Check whether an Official Journal-referenced cybersecurity scheme covers the relevant Article 15 requirements.

concepts.name: CRA interplay lookup
concepts.assessment: Locate the CRA scope, deemed-compliance conditions and assessment interplay before accepting a cybersecurity compliance claim.

concepts.name: Standards update watch
concepts.assessment: Record version, coverage, citation and procedure changes that require a fresh release review.

concepts.name: International certificate boundary
concepts.assessment: Explain why an ISO management-system certificate or a supplier assertion alone does not establish AI Act conformity.

concepts.name: Conformity evidence case
concepts.assessment: Find the coverage gap in a fictional certification pitch and request the evidence needed to resolve it.

concepts.name: Notifying authority
concepts.assessment: Distinguish the authority designating and monitoring assessors from the assessor reviewing the product.

concepts.name: Notified body
concepts.assessment: Distinguish a designated conformity assessor from a consultant or ordinary certification provider.

concepts.name: Notified scope verification
concepts.assessment: Check the body identification, notified task and system codes, status and any third-country agreement basis.

concepts.name: Designation evidence
concepts.assessment: Distinguish accreditation, other designation evidence and the Article 32 presumption for a body from product compliance.

concepts.name: Notification objection window
concepts.assessment: Distinguish the two-week and two-month objection windows and their effect on notification.

concepts.name: Unified sector designation
concepts.assessment: Recognise when a sector law permits unified designation and what evidence is needed for transitional assessment powers.

concepts.name: Assessor independence
concepts.assessment: Identify an assessor conflict or resource/process failure that undermines the required independent assessment.

concepts.name: Assessor confidentiality
concepts.assessment: Distinguish confidentiality protection from refusal to provide lawfully required assessment evidence.

concepts.name: Assessor competence
concepts.assessment: Match the assessment scope to staff competence, methods, records and conformity-assessment experience.

concepts.name: Subcontracting accountability
concepts.assessment: Identify the consent, qualification, record and responsibility conditions for an assessor subcontractor.

concepts.name: Proportionate assessment
concepts.assessment: Distinguish proportionate assessment effort from lowering protection or omitting an applicable requirement.

concepts.name: Designation change response
concepts.assessment: Identify the certificate, file-transfer and continuity checks triggered by designation restriction, withdrawal or cessation.

concepts.name: Competence challenge
concepts.assessment: Locate the Commission challenge and corrective procedure when assessor competence is disputed.

concepts.name: Assessor coordination
concepts.assessment: Identify the purpose of information exchange and coordination without treating it as a new product authorisation.

concepts.name: Assessor selection case
concepts.assessment: Select or reject a fictional assessor using scope, independence, subcontracting and continuity evidence.

concepts.name: Internal control assessment
concepts.assessment: Specify the provider checks for Annex III points 2–8 without adding an AI Act notified-body requirement.

concepts.name: Design file consistency
concepts.assessment: Check whether design, development and post-market monitoring agree with the assessed technical documentation.

concepts.name: Biometric assessment route
concepts.assessment: Distinguish the Annex VI/Annex VII choice from mandatory Annex VII when standards or common-specification conditions fail.

concepts.name: Special authority assessor
concepts.assessment: Identify when the specified market surveillance authority acts as the notified body for the assessment.

concepts.name: QMS approval
concepts.assessment: Prepare the quality-management application and route a proposed QMS change for the required decision.

concepts.name: Technical documentation assessment
concepts.assessment: Identify the application, necessary data/testing evidence, restricted model-access conditions and refusal/retraining consequences.

concepts.name: QMS surveillance
concepts.assessment: Identify the ongoing premises access, information and periodic-audit duties after QMS approval.

concepts.name: Certificate lifecycle
concepts.assessment: Check validity, reassessment, supplement dependency, corrective action, restriction, suspension, withdrawal and appeal.

concepts.name: Assessment result sharing
concepts.assessment: Distinguish notifications to authorities from exchanges with other bodies and preserve confidentiality.

concepts.name: Substantial modification test
concepts.assessment: Evaluate whether a change requires a new assessment, including continued use by the same deployer and changed provider duties.

concepts.name: Predetermined learning change
concepts.assessment: Distinguish initially documented predetermined learning changes from an unrestricted exemption for later model updates.

concepts.name: Assessment route case
concepts.assessment: Defend the HR, biometric and stipulated medical-product procedures and resolve a proposed post-assessment change.

concepts.name: Conformity derogation authorisation
concepts.assessment: Identify a justified, authority-granted, territorially and temporally limited derogation while Section 2 compliance remains required.

concepts.name: Emergency use boundary
concepts.assessment: Identify the narrowly specified urgent law-enforcement/civil-protection conditions, immediate request and refusal consequences.

concepts.name: Sector derogation boundary
concepts.assessment: Use the relevant product-law derogation for an Annex I Section A product instead of treating Article 46 as a general shortcut.

concepts.name: Provider declaration responsibility
concepts.assessment: Identify provider responsibility, machine-readable signed form, authority language, ten-year retention, updates and combined-law declaration.

concepts.name: Declaration content check
concepts.assessment: Check the eight declaration fields and evidence for any applicable personal-data statement; a signature does not prove compliance.

concepts.name: CE marking accessibility
concepts.assessment: Select digital access and visible, legible, indelible marking or the specified fallback, including other applicable CE laws.

concepts.name: CE notified body number
concepts.assessment: Identify when the body identification number accompanies marking and promotional mentions, without inventing a body for internal control.

concepts.name: Registration role test
concepts.assessment: Decide who registers before market/service, including a non-high-risk Article 6(3) conclusion; registration does not confer approval.

concepts.name: High risk registration record
concepts.assessment: Prepare the provider fields, conditional certificate attachments, declaration and instructions with their specified exceptions.

concepts.name: Exempt system registration record
concepts.assessment: Prepare the non-high-risk record using the remaining fields and recognise that points 7 and 9 were deleted.

concepts.name: Registration destination test
concepts.assessment: Choose the EU public, secured non-public or national registration destination for the stated system and context.

concepts.name: Public deployer registration
concepts.assessment: Identify the specified public/Union/acting-on-behalf deployer duty and its fields without extending it to every private deployer.

concepts.name: Market release case
concepts.assessment: Make a supported ready/not-ready/needs-specialist-review decision with a dated route record, remaining evidence gaps and change controls.

edges.reason: Classification attaches to the defined system and intended purpose.
The prohibited-practice check needs the actual intended function and context.
The date lookup distinguishes the system route and applicable section.
The transition test needs the relevant application dates and dated release facts.
Sector assessment can only be selected after distinguishing the Annex I route and its scope limits.
The combined case needs an identified applicable sector procedure.
The evidence map must start from the requirements applicable to the chosen route.
The dossier must identify which version and system its records describe.
The index must connect system records to the requirement evidence already identified.
A release scope conclusion cannot ignore a prohibition.
The dated case must distinguish a new release from an existing-system transition.
The medical case needs the procedure priority when routes overlap.
The case needs a defined evidence dossier before it can record unresolved release gaps.
The presumption depends on the legally cited version and restrictions.
A gap analysis needs the boundary of the presumption being claimed.
A standard cannot be mapped to coverage without the applicable requirements.
Alternative evidence must address the identified uncovered requirement.
The equivalence justification concerns an identified applicable common specification.
The equivalent solution must cover the requirement left unresolved by the chosen conformity evidence.
The data presumption must be limited to its particular requirement.
A cybersecurity certificate must be evaluated as a limited presumption.
The CRA bridge is a distinct route to the cybersecurity requirement, not all AI Act duties.
A version watch needs the precise citation and restrictions being monitored.
The certificate claim must be evaluated against the actual legal coverage boundary.
The case must specify evidence for the identified gap.
The common-specification claim requires a reasoned equivalence check.
The case includes a cybersecurity certificate with limited coverage.
The scope check concerns a formally designated assessor, not a consultant.
Designation evidence establishes the qualification of the conformity assessor.
The effective notification window depends on the type of supporting designation evidence.
Unified designation depends on the relevant sector law and assessment scope.
Existing sector designation evidence must be distinguished from new AI Act designation.
The independence requirement applies to the body carrying out conformity assessment.
The competence review must match the tasks and system types in scope.
Subcontracting must preserve the required independence.
The body remains accountable for subcontractor qualifications.
Proportionate effort cannot remove a requirement from the evidence matrix.
Continuity decisions depend on the formal assessor status that has changed.
The selected assessor must be qualified for the actual task and system codes.
An otherwise qualified assessor must still pass the conflict check.
The case includes a subcontractor whose responsibility and consent need checking.
The case needs a response to a changed designation after selection.
The internal-control duty depends on the relevant Annex III points and route.
Internal assessment needs the applicable requirements and supporting evidence.
Consistency is one of the provider checks within internal control.
Consistency must be checked against the identified technical records.
The special procedure is limited to the relevant Annex III point 1 systems.
The procedure choice depends on applied standards/common-specification coverage and restrictions.
The authority-as-assessor condition applies within this biometric Annex VII procedure.
The application is submitted to the legally qualified assessment body.
QMS approval needs documented procedures and evidence of the applicable requirements.
The technical application must concern a system within the relevant quality-management approval.
The assessor needs the system-specific technical file and its evidence.
Surveillance checks continued compliance with the approved QMS.
Certificate management begins with the assessed system and reasoned decision.
The notifications distinguish issued, refused, restricted and withdrawn assessment outcomes.
The sharing duty must preserve the applicable confidentiality rules.
The change test compares the current system and purpose with the initially assessed version.
The predetermined-change rule is a bounded exception within the modification test.
The exception needs changes recorded in the initial technical documentation.
The HR case requires the provider internal-control procedure.
The biometric case requires the standards-dependent assessment branch.
The case requires evidence and access decisions under an external assessment.
The case includes a change after the initial assessment.
The request is a derogation from the otherwise applicable high-risk assessment procedure.
The urgent-use rule is a narrow exception to obtaining assessment derogation authorisation first.
The sector boundary distinguishes the applicable derogation authorisation route.
Annex I Section A products use their relevant sector-law derogations.
The provider needs conformity evidence before accepting responsibility for the declaration.
The content check concerns the signed declaration for which the provider takes responsibility.
Declaration fields must trace to the specific system and version.
CE marking follows the conformity conclusion and provider declaration.
The number rule concerns how the required CE marking is presented.
A body number must identify the appropriate notified assessor where the route requires it.
Registration distinguishes an Annex III system, an Article 6(3) conclusion and other routes.
The actor test needs the provider responsible for registration.
The fields depend on the applicable provider registration category.
The high-risk record includes the relevant EU declaration of conformity.
The non-high-risk registration fields depend on a documented Article 6(3) conclusion.
The destination lookup starts with the applicable actor/system registration duty.
The deployer record is distinct from the provider registration duty.
The final release decision needs a supported assessment-route conclusion.
The final dossier needs the required declaration content and supporting evidence.
The final release needs a valid marking and access decision.
The final release needs the applicable registration destination and recorded gaps.
The overview helps locate the scope record without being needed to define a system.
The authority/body contrast is useful context; the body can still be defined on its own.
The citation check helps contrast standards with implementing-act specifications.
The assessor role supplies context for confidentiality but is not necessary to understand the evidence-sharing boundary.
Status-change consequences help explain why competence challenges matter.
The body role helps situate coordination without making it a conceptual gate.
Check for changed procedures before relying on the case route in a real release.
An exceptional-release proposal must use the correct sector route and specialist review.
The public-authority case variation adds a deployer record beyond the provider release.
A separate product cybersecurity law may require an additional procedure even where the AI Act route is internal control.
